label: Free 2.0
title: Purposes, a consent webhook and a safe upgrade
lede: Permito 2.0 adds purposes as a first-class idea next to categories, plus a webhook that tells your own backend when someone changes or withdraws consent. Visitors who consented under 1.x are not asked again.

items.title: Purposes next to categories
items.text: Split a category into purposes with stable IDs, then check or decline a single purpose without touching the rest of its category.
items.output:
newsletter: true
retargeting: true
after decline -> retargeting: false
purposes: {"newsletter":true,"retargeting":false,"necessary":true}

items.title: Consent webhook
items.text: connectConsentWebhook posts every change to your own URL, including which purposes were withdrawn. parseConsentWebhookPayload validates it on the server.
items.outputTitle: Payload the receiver gets after a withdrawal (trimmed)

items.title: 1.x decisions keep working
items.text: A consent stored by Permito 1.x is migrated to the new schema when it loads, so returning visitors are not asked again.

items.title: Purposes in React
items.text: @permitojs/react exports useHasPurposeConsent to gate UI by purpose.
items.code:
import { useHasPurposeConsent } from "@permitojs/react";

const allowed = useHasPurposeConsent("newsletter");

note: Outputs were produced by running these scripts against @permitojs/core 2.0.0 from npm. Node 22 or newer is required.
